tmu.title: TMU Business Network
tmu.lede: I co-founded The Master's University's official networking society and grew it from zero to 650+ members — more than half the student body — in three months.
meta: The Master's University · Santa Clarita, CA
tmu.challenge: Connect a campus of about 1,200 students with working professionals in respected fields — starting with zero members and no events.
approach: Give people a reason to join
A clear offer: time with a working professional through coffee chats, Zoom meetings and one-on-one matching.
Meet students where they are
Campus-fair booths, weekly event bulletins, online invites and social outreach, run in person and across channels.
Keep a steady cadence
One to two events a week, averaging about 20 attendees each.
Build the industry pipeline
Matched 10+ students with professionals from Big Four firms including Deloitte, EY and KPMG.
tmu.takeaway: Growing a community runs like a sales funnel: reach people where they already are, make one clear offer, and repeat it on a schedule they can count on.
tmu.imageAlt: Growth card: 0 to 650+ members in 3 months, 54% of campus; coffee chats, Zoom and 1:1 matching; partners Deloitte, EY, KPMG
tmu.summary: Co-founded the university’s official networking society and grew it with weekly events, campus-fair booths, bulletins and social outreach.
outcomes: 10+ students matched with Deloitte, EY and KPMG pros

fieldnote.title: Fieldnote
fieldnote.lede: A fresh-filled cologne brand for college students. I took it from a name to a business plan to a live storefront at fieldnotela.com.
fieldnote.challenge: Fragrance is usually sold as a finished bottle off a shelf. Fieldnote's idea: fill each bottle the day it's ordered and label it with the buyer's name, city and fill date — at a price that works for students.
approach: Name and position it
Chose the name Fieldnote and built the brand around one promise: made the day you order it.
Plan the business
A full plan covering market sizing, competitive analysis, marketing, operations and a three-year financial model.
Design the storefront in Figma
A warm editorial system — espresso, bone, linen and a clay accent — with product pages, a discovery set and a photo guide.
Ship it, then test demand
A live site with six house scents and a label builder. Next: 2ml sample packs to measure real demand before making house scents.
fieldnote.takeaway: Validate before you scale: the site and brand are real, but the next step is proving people want it — with sample packs, before any inventory.
fieldnote.imageAlt: The Fieldnote storefront homepage: “Made the day you order it.”
fieldnote.summary: A fresh-filled cologne brand for college students, taken from name to business plan to a live storefront at fieldnotela.com.
outcomes: Named, positioned and planned the brand end to end
Designed the full storefront system in Figma
Shipped a live site with a custom label builder

close.title: The Close
close.lede: How I sell. One framework, used across university recruitment, high-ticket coaching and gym memberships.
meta: Recruitment associate · Sales closer · Lead service specialist
close.challenge: Three very different sales motions — cold calls to prospective students, high-ticket coaching calls, and walk-in gym tours — with the same job: turn interest into a decision.
approach: I · Discovery
Open by surfacing the prospect's pain points and goals.
II · The offer
Present the offer against the needs they just described.
III · Benefit stack
Stack the benefits so the value is clear.
IV · Urgency
Use loss aversion and scarcity to move toward a decision.
V · Same-call decision
Ask for the commitment on the call.
close.takeaway: Cold-calling across California, Arizona and Texas using the 7 P’s; closing high-ticket coaching offers on commission; and converting leads and walk-ins at Fitness 19 while meeting or exceeding monthly targets.
close.imageAlt: The close, in five moves: Discovery, The offer, Benefit stack, Urgency, Same-call decision
close.summary: How I sell: discovery first, then the offer against stated goals, then urgency. Used in gym memberships, high-ticket coaching and university recruitment.
outcomes: High-ticket offers closed from a 14K-follower audience
